items.text: scripts/export_invoices.py was added for the Finance team (usage: `python scripts/export_invoices.py DB_PATH OUT_CSV`). It reads the `invoices` table of a tinydb db.json, opened read-only, and writes one CSV row per invoice with columns number, customer, amount, due_date; missing fields become empty cells and amounts are written as stored. The output is semicolon-separated with a UTF-8 BOM so it opens correctly in Excel with a German locale. It imports tinydb (needs `pip install tinydb` or PYTHONPATH=.). A sample db is at scripts/sample/db.json (includes INV-004 'Müller GmbH'). The script keeps its own CSV writer rather than using `Table.to_csv`, which writes plain comma-separated UTF-8; the agent offered (2026-11-04) to add `delimiter` and `encoding` options to `to_csv` and migrate the script if Finance needs the Excel format everywhere, but no decision was made.

Four tests for `Table.to_csv` were added in `tests/test_tables.py` (default columns, selected and reordered columns, empty table, quoting plus non-ASCII text); the full suite passed (236 tests). pytest had to be run with `-c /dev/null` because `pytest.ini` requires coverage options unavailable in that environment. The changes are uncommitted on the `table-to-csv` branch (2026-11-04).

items.text: `Table.to_csv(path, fields=None)` was added in `tinydb/table.py` on 2026-11-04 at the request of the Finance team, who repeatedly ask for CSV dumps of tables. It writes a header row then one row per document, as UTF-8 comma-separated text, overwriting an existing file. `fields` selects and orders columns and defaults to every top-level key in first-seen order; missing values become empty cells and keys not in `fields` are ignored. An empty table with no `fields` yields an empty file; with `fields` it yields only the header.

items.text: TinyDB v4.0 was a major architecture refactor (rationale in #284, November 2019): Python 2 support, ujson support and the deprecated element ID API were removed, and a new architecture was introduced (closes #250, #103) with type annotations and subclassing helpers (Extension Mechanisms). Goal: simplify and modernize the codebase and enable extension mechanisms. Table was reworked in Jan-Feb 2020: it stores the next ID instead of the last ID, process_docs was removed, internal read/update methods were renamed, len(table) performance improved, and Table.contains accepts only a single doc ID because list semantics were ambiguous. Queries refactor (2020-02-19): evaluating queries without a test was dropped (breaking change), and regexes handle non-string values correctly. v4.0.0 was released 2020-05-02 with upgrade notes, changelog and updated docs; follow-up fixes for counting docs in an empty db (#307) and next document ID calculation on existing tables (#314) shipped in 4.0.x/4.1.0.
v3.12.0 was released on 2018-11-06 by Markus Siemens (commit c3553af, 'Version bump to v3.12.0'); it was followed by the v3.12.1 patch release three days later.

September 2026 robustness fixes: CachingMiddleware rejects reads/writes after close (#634); auto-ids no longer collide in mixed insert_multiple batches (#633); LRUCache no longer treats stored None values as missing, using a private sentinel for presence checks (#635). Goal: prevent data corruption and incorrect cache semantics.

Atomic writes to avoid data corruption on crashes were attempted in May 2022 (2a2abe5, #468, Stefano Scafiti) but reverted (5694479) after CI failures; a Windows atomic write fix (cbeaf5c) was also made. CI was extended to macOS and Windows, excluding Windows+PyPy3 and macOS+PyPy3.
